To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the methods of searching for TF binding sites can be divided into two groups: the methods based on a single TFBS model and the methods based on several TFBS models, and the methods based only on a single TF binding site model are not able to find all the TF binding sites in a genome.

the performance of a binding site search method is determined primarily by the quality of its model of transcription factor binding, that the best models of binding are obtained using a combination of phylogenetic footprinting and position-specific weight matrices, and that the most effective way to represent binding site models is to use a mixture of position-specific weight matrices.

the use of multiple sequence alignment methods to represent transcription factor binding sites is superior to the use of consensus sequences and that the use of position-specific scoring matrices is superior to the representation of transcription factor binding sites by position-specific scoring matrices and the use of position weight matrices is superior to both.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to represent and search for transcription factor binding site motifs in DNA sequences.
the development of methods to represent and search for regulatory motifs in DNA.
the development and evaluation of methods for the prediction and discovery of regulatory elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no best method, and the best method is the one that works for you.
there is a clear need for a standard format to store information about TFBSs, and that this should be a simple format that can be used by all groups.
, at present, there is not a single best approach for identifying and analyzing transcription factor binding sites in DNA sequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most accurate methods for predicting transcription factor binding sites (TFBS) are those that use a hidden Markov model (HMM), and that these HMMs are trained using a combination of phylogenetic footprinting (PF) and phylogenetic shadowing (PS) data.
there is no one best method for representing and searching DNA for transcription factor binding site (TFBS) motifs.
the most important factor in the success of any binding site search method is the quality and size of the training set of known binding sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the most part, the methods we compared performed similarly.
the best way of searching for binding sites is to use the PWMs that are derived from the binding sites themselves, rather than from the sequences that the TF is known to bind to.
the best method for finding binding sites is to use the best available motif model, and then to use that motif to search for binding sites.
